rules.label: Whether a pop-up box includes its modules
rules.guidance:
A pop-up or floor box line is priced one of two ways, and the first thing to decide is
which.

Read the line as INCLUDING modules only when it actually supplies them - when it
enumerates sockets, switches, chargers or outlets that sit in the box, or says the box is
supplied populated, loaded, fitted or complete with them. Set Includes modules to Yes and
fill in the module attributes for what it names.

Read the line as WITHOUT modules when it supplies the box alone - the enclosure, the
lid, the frame, the mounting arrangement - with nothing named inside it. Set Includes
modules to No and return None for every module attribute: the switch, all four sockets,
the blank plate and the face plate. Colour is not a module attribute: leave it to its
default unless the row names one.

Language that anticipates modules is not the same as supplying them. A box described as
having provision to take, being suitable for, shall support, can accommodate, or is
designed for a number of modules is a box WITHOUT modules - it states a capacity, not
contents. So is a line that explicitly excludes them, such as modules to be supplied
separately, box to exclude the modules, or modules by others. In every one of those cases
answer No.

A module count on its own is a capacity too. A twelve module pop-up box is a twelve
module enclosure; it does not tell you that twelve modules are being supplied.

When the line does include modules but names something the catalog does not carry, fill
in the parts you can read and leave the rest blank rather than forcing a wrong match.

Leave Includes modules blank only when the line genuinely does not say either way.

rules.label: Industrial socket paired MCB
rules.guidance: Industrial socket lines are often billed together with the MCB that controls them. Report what the line SAYS about that MCB; the pairing itself is computed downstream. (0) `paired_mcb`: ALWAYS return null for this attribute, even when the text names a specific MCB - the pairing is computed downstream from the facts you report. (1) `mcb_present`: "Yes" only when the text itself NAMES a breaker. The row's `description`, its `notes`, or an `ancestor_chain` entry must contain the word MCB - or an unambiguous equivalent: MCCB, RCBO, RCCB, ELCB, "miniature circuit breaker", "circuit breaker". A word must actually be present: this is a reading test, not a judgement. The following are NOT mentions, and each of them on its own means "No": an incomer or incoming supply; any current or amperage figure, including the socket's own rating; a distribution board, trolley, panel or feeder context; internal wiring; protection implied by the kind of equipment described. When no such word appears, answer "No". If you are unsure, answer "No" - a socket priced without an MCB is corrected in one click, a socket priced with an MCB nobody asked for is invisible. (2) `mcb_amp_a`: if the text states a current specifically for the MCB, use it; otherwise the HIGHEST current stated anywhere in the text (a socket's stated current serves the MCB when no separate MCB current is given). '25/20/16 A' gives 25. Read it from the text itself, never from the `rating` attribute, whose values are ranges that lose the individual figures. Leave it blank only when the text states no current at all. (3) `mcb_pole_stated`: the pole DESIGNATION the text uses for the MCB, recorded VERBATIM as one of the allowed values - do not convert it. 'TPN', 'TP+N', 'TP+NL', 'TP+2N' and 'TP+2NL' each mean four pole and must be recorded exactly as the text writes them, never shortened to 'TP' and never to a shorter one of each other; the conversion to the catalogue's pole is computed downstream from what you report. Leave it "None" when the text does not state one; do not infer it from the socket's pin count. (4) `mcb_curve_stated`: the curve the text states (C or D). Leave it "None" when none is stated. Steps (2), (3) and (4) describe the MCB only when `mcb_present` is "Yes". When you answered "No", return `mcb_amp_a` blank and `mcb_pole_stated` / `mcb_curve_stated` as "None" - there is no MCB to describe, so there is nothing to read. Deciding (1) is not a consequence of being able to answer (2): a current figure in the text is never evidence that an MCB exists.

point_wiring.notes: LIVE at EA-4a (2026-07-30): the assembly pipelines encode the guiding PW block FAITHFULLY - per-line UNIT rounding (differs from the standalone category blocks' tens rounding: switch 155 here vs 160 standalone - INTENTIONAL, per the sheet); every component references the live master rows (component_ref + rate_stages x qty); circuit_fit computes fitted conduit + circuits. Oracle: 1869/735 (+BCS 1370) banked at EA-3. Multiplier provenance: wires K4 0.602 / M4 0.4515 / install x(1+I6=1.0); conduit H3 0.7 / I3 0.5 / F4 0.2; switches L 0.3625 / M 0.25 / J7 0.2 (uniform across families, verified 2026-07-30). | EA-4a-r (2026-07-31): None mechanism. socket/switch/plate/wire2 are allow_none; selecting None disables the dependent inputs (qty; wire2 core; plate None ALSO disables back_box since the box is keyed by plate size) and the line contributes ZERO; circuit_fit omits wire2 from the dia when wire2=None (single-wire point). None = positive absence (distinct from blank=unknown); extraction returns None when an enumerated bill names no such component, blank when the row is vague. | PW-CONDUIT-OPTIONAL + LENGTH-BY-POINT-TYPE (v50): the conduit is now droppable and the circuit length can be substituted. THE CONDUIT DECISION IS CODE, NEVER THE MODEL: the model reports three facts (conduit_handoff / other_conduit / conduit_price_excluded, all panel:false) and a three-step map_attribute chain applies the owner's decision table. DROP happens on exactly three shapes - an explicit price exclusion; a handed-off run with no other conduit; a handed-off run whose only other conduit is FLEXIBLE. EVERYTHING ELSE INCLUDES PVC, including the slash alternation and silence. *** OPPOSITE DEFAULTS, BY DESIGN: wiring_cabling (F-28) maps conduit_included default 'No' - a CABLE row silent on conduit EXCLUDES it. point_wiring maps default 'Yes' - a POINT WIRING row silent on conduit INCLUDES PVC. Point wiring normally carries conduit; cables normally do not. DO NOT HARMONISE THEM: a future editor who makes them agree breaks one. *** ERROR DIRECTION: a wrong reading here UNDER-quotes, silently, and nothing on screen says a component was skipped - the mirror of the cable case, where a wrong reading over-quoted and a human noticed. That is why every ambiguous shape includes. circuit_length_m: point_type Primary -> 15 m, Secondary -> 5 m, anything else leaves the 15 + (points-1)*5 formula standing. rules.label: Wire runs, cores, and the number of points in point wiring
rules.guidance:
Report the wire specification EXACTLY AS THE LINE STATES IT. Do not add,
complete or balance anything: if the line gives one wire, report one wire; if
it gives a run count, report that count, whatever it is.

Read the line as follows.

When a run count is stated, such as 3R x 1.5 sqmm, record it as given: 3 runs,
1 core.

When a size is given with a plain multiplier and no run marker, such as
3 x 1.5 sqmm, the multiplier is the run count: 3 runs, 1 core, 1.5 sqmm.

When only a size is given with no multiplier at all, such as 1.5 sqmm, record
1 run of 1 core at that size -- the line states no count, so do not invent one.

In each of those cases, look for a second conductor named separately - an
earth wire, or any further size - before deciding there is only one wire. A
separately named earth wire IS a second wire: record the first size as wire 1
with the runs the line gives it, and the named earth as wire 2 with its own.

When the line states two different run counts, such as two runs of 2.5 sqmm
and one run of 1.5 sqmm, record the wire with the higher run count as wire 1
and the lower as wire 2.

When the line gives two sizes with no run counts at all, record the larger
size as wire 1 and the smaller as wire 2, ONE run each -- the line states no
counts, so do not invent them. Which is larger still decides the order.

Record a core count greater than 1 only when the line positively states
multiple cores - 2C, two core, 3 core. A number before the size is a run
count, not a core count.

Also record the NUMBER OF POINTS the line covers. A line reading Set of seven
(7) light points covers 7; Three (3) light point covers 3; a line describing a
single outlet or a single socket on a breaker covers 1. Where the line names
no count at all, record 1. Count the points the line prices, not the number of
such lines in the bill.

rules.label: What the row says about conduit
rules.guidance:
A point wiring line often says what the wiring runs through. Report only what the document says and never infer a value it does not give. Never decide whether the conduit should be priced - that decision is made elsewhere from your answers.

conduit_handoff: answer Yes when the document says this run uses something already there - a raceway, a cable tray, trunking, or an existing conduit. Answer Either ONLY when the document offers a choice between two DIFFERENT CONTAINERS - a conduit versus a raceway, a tray, or trunking - for example 'in existing conduit / raceway'. A slash between anything else is NOT a choice of container and must NOT be read as Either. Such a slash almost always describes how the conduit is MOUNTED, and how a conduit is mounted says nothing about who supplies it.
Decide this field by ONE TEST: does the document say the conduit is ALREADY THERE? Only words to that effect -- that it is existing, already laid, already provided, previously installed, or supplied under another item -- make it already there. If such a word is present, answer Yes. If the line merely DESCRIBES a conduit -- how it is mounted, its gauge, material, size, grade or make -- and nothing anywhere says it is already there, then this line supplies that conduit and the answer is No. The same test applies to a slash between sizes, materials, grades or makes.
This field is ONLY about who supplies the conduit. It is not about the wiring, and nothing you decide here should change any other answer. Answer No when the run uses a conduit this line supplies. Leave it unstated when the line says nothing about what the wiring runs through.

other_conduit: answer Flexible when the only other conduit the line names is a flexible one, for example a flexible conduit at the drop of a light fixture. Answer Normal when it names an ordinary rigid conduit somewhere other than the run itself. Answer None when it names no other conduit. Leave it unstated when you cannot tell.

conduit_price_excluded: answer Yes ONLY when the document plainly says the conduit's price is not in this rate - for example 'conduit shall be paid under separate line item', 'the cost should be exclusive of conduits', 'conduit by others'. Answer No when it says the conduit cost IS included. Leave it unstated when the document does not address the conduit's price. Beware the opposite polarity: 'cost of conduit is included' is NOT an exclusion.

rules.label: Whether the rate includes the circuit wiring, and what that circuit wire is
rules.applies_to: circuit_wire_included, circuit_wire1_core, circuit_wire1_runs, circuit_wire1_thickness_sqmm, circuit_wire2_core, circuit_wire2_runs, circuit_wire2_thickness_sqmm
rules.guidance:
Some point wiring lines also cover the CIRCUIT (submain) wiring that feeds the point -- the run from the distribution board to the switch board or to the first point. That is a different conductor from the point wiring itself, and it is priced separately. Report only what the document says and never infer a value it does not give. Never decide whether the circuit wiring should be charged -- that decision is made elsewhere from your answers.

circuit_wire_included: answer Yes ONLY when the line POSITIVELY says its rate covers that run -- for example 'including circuit wiring from the DB', 'the rate shall include wiring from the distribution board to the switch board', 'inclusive of circuit main'. A heading that merely DESCRIBES the point wiring, even one naming a distribution board and a wire size, is NOT such a statement: 'Primary Light / Fan Point Circuit Wiring Controlled from DB with 2.5 sqmm x 3 Wire' describes what the point wiring IS, and the answer there is No. Answer No when the line says nothing about a separate circuit run, and No when it puts that run outside this rate ('circuit wiring paid under a separate item', 'excluding circuit main'). SILENCE IS No: the line must carry positive inclusion language.

circuit_wire1_core / circuit_wire1_runs / circuit_wire1_thickness_sqmm and the wire 2 equivalents: these describe the CIRCUIT wire, not the point wire. Read them from whatever the line says about the run from the distribution board, using the same reading conventions R9 gives for the point wiring. Where the line names circuit wiring but gives no size for it, leave the thickness BLANK -- never "None".

hvac_insulation.notes: SLICE 12a (owner I-1): the CATALOGUE and the MECHANISM. Pricing, extraction and the panel are 12b, which is why `pipelines` is empty -- `config_is_eligible` needs pipelines AND definitions, so no BoQ screen changes. The cost parts are stored SEPARATELY and never baked (owner I-3: a row's own parts stay editable); an unclad row stores cost_cladding 0 explicitly. 24G is the same rate as 26G (owner I-10) and differs only in the gauge. SLICE 12c: the pricing RULES, in `list_spec` only -- `pipelines` stays EMPTY so the category is still not eligible and every Insulation BoQ row keeps its coming-soon card (Q13). Cladding is computed from the seven HVAC Pricing Inputs, so `cost_cladding` is no longer stored on the pipe rows. SLICE 12c FINISH: the five CLADDING-ONLY SKUs (owner F1) -- one per cladding type, priced from the ROW'S own pipe size and thickness by the composites' own cladding formula, wastage included. A per-sq.m cladding-only row takes the plain sheet rate with NO overlap (owner F2). FA7 (owner ruling 2026-10-04, option A): `calculator_only` admits this category to the Pricing CALCULATOR tab only -- BoQ rows still show the coming-soon card and the category stays out of the extraction population. TEMPORARY: the slice that makes Insulation fully eligible REMOVES this key in the same slice, so there is never a second on/off switch. Owner 2026-10-04: every attribute is a DROPDOWN built from the active catalogue rows (`panel_controls`), so adding a catalogue item adds its option with no code change. Owner C-R1/C-R2/C-R3 2026-10-04: the pipe size resolves FIRST so a composition is built from ONE pipe size's rows, and a tie that closeness cannot break goes to the lowest summed cost_insulation.

attributes.name: Cable tray supply markup
attributes.remarks: The margin on a cable tray's supply rate. A Ladder, MS powder-coated tray at Rs 290/m is quoted at Rs 420.50/m.

attributes.remarks: The margin on earthing supply. A GI 50 x 10 mm earth strip at Rs 312 is quoted at Rs 452.40.

attributes.name: Lighting management system supply markup
attributes.remarks: An LMS catalogue rate is our cost. The quote is the rate + 30%, rounded up to the nearest 10. A Rs 24,500 Lutron panel is quoted at Rs 31,850.

attributes.remarks: An LMS catalogue rate is our cost with nothing added. The Rs 24,500 Lutron panel costs us Rs 24,500. Raise this and every LMS cost rises.

attributes.remarks: The margin on a junction box. A 250 mm face box lists at Rs 410 and is quoted at Rs 594.50.

attributes.name: Cable tray floor-cutting installation markup

attributes.name: Cable installation markup
attributes.remarks: A stored cable install cost is billed at double. A 4-core copper armoured cable's Rs 22/m install cost is billed at Rs 44/m.

attributes.name: Earthing installation markup
attributes.remarks: A stored earthing install cost takes a 45% margin. A CU 32 x 3 mm strip's Rs 44 install cost is billed at Rs 63.80.

attributes.name: Cable tray installation markup
attributes.remarks: A cable tray's stored install rate is billed with no margin added. A Perforated GI 1.2 mm tray's Rs 220/m is billed at Rs 220/m. Raise this and every tray install rate rises with it.

attributes.remarks: A Misc catalogue rate is the quote; our cost is this share of it. Rubber Mat quotes Rs 3,200 and costs Rs 2,560.
